subject.title: feat: MCP Apps (ui://) Phase 0 — generic host in Control UI + plugin-declared MCP servers

question: Should MCP Apps ship only with the production different-origin proxy and a deny-by-default privileged-permission policy, and should `mcpServers` become a permanent native plugin manifest contract?
rationale: The shipped CSP and upstream host model make the proxy architectural rather than optional, while browser capability consent and a new external plugin API require maintainer intent that tests cannot determine.

options.title: Complete generic host first
options.body: Implement and prove the production proxy, initially deny privileged browser permissions, and approve `mcpServers` with focused compatibility tests.

options.title: Split protocol plumbing
options.body: Remove the browser renderer and manifest API, then propose only independently useful MCP metadata and resource handling in a narrower PR.

options.title: Pause the proposal
options.body: Keep the draft paused until the security architecture and plugin API ownership have an approved design.

recommendation.title: Complete generic host first
recommendation.body: Implement and prove the production proxy, initially deny privileged browser permissions, and approve `mcpServers` with focused compatibility tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows the broadest ownership across the affected MCP runtime, plugin manifest, Control UI, and gateway CSP decision surfaces.
